properties.name: The first frequency x cost ranking of the tool surface — three things are 68% of all measured tool time, and the long tail of writes is ~120 ms each
properties.statement:
Anthony's rule for the optimisation campaign, 2026-09-12: "if a tool is used 500x compared to one used 5x, focus on the 500x tool." The under-1s goal is an OBJECTIVE, not a threshold. This is the first ranking built to that rule, and it needed two instruments joined: FREQUENCY from tools/surface_usage.py over every retained transcript (47 sessions, 9,335 calls, 154 of 181 tools, 8 projects; reflow2's own self-host is 7,472 of those calls, musicjug 1,012, six others under 250 each), and COST from a controlled per-tool measurement on a copy of the live store (0.59.0 release, quiet box, medians of 3), with reads measured both cold (first after a write) and warm, and the post-write tax attributed by the real write->read transition counts.

TOP BY VOLUME (share of all calls): add_decision 680 (7.3%), get_node 645, export_graph 579, create_node 553, search_design 495, authored_by 455, loop_status 331 (3.5%, but in 44 of 47 sessions), set_artifact_checksum 249, create_edge 245, add_change_event 243. The top 10 are 48% of calls; the top 40 are 85%.

TOP BY VOLUME x COST (share of ~1,717 s measured), warm figures for reads:
  1. loop_status        ~54%  (331 calls; 1.3-2.4 s warm, ~4.1 s after a write, so the true share is higher)
  2. export_graph       ~30%  (579 calls x ~1,010 ms — it serialises a 16 MB record every time)
  3. the post-write tax ~27% of the pre-export total (417 occurrences x ~1.1 s; fact:the-first-store-read-after-any-write-pays-a-fixed-1-1s-tax-whichever-tool-it-is) — it is the ENTIRE cost of get_node (#2 by volume) and search_design (#5), whose own cost is 1-2 ms
  4. add_decision        82 s  (680 x 121 ms)
  5. set_artifact_checksum 67 s (249 x 271 ms)
  6. create_node         64 s  (553 x 116 ms)
  7. detect_defects      56 s  (52 x 734 ms warm / 1,644 cold)
  8. review_relations    33 s, add_change_event 28 s, set_decision_status 24 s, add_capability 24 s, add_requirement 24 s
(shares overlap because export_graph's own cost was mis-stripped in the first pass and is restated here; the ordering is robust to it.)

THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS FOR PRIORITISING. Everything below the top three is a WRITE at 110-350 ms per call (add_decision 121, create_node 116, add_capability 116, add_requirement 126, add_change_event 117, add_verification 123, set_decision_status 135, set_verification_status 150, set_requirement_status 178, record_change ~300, link_artifact 248, set_artifact_checksum 271, add_epoch 253) and every RELATION tool is ~1 ms (authored_by, satisfies, allocate, verifies, governed_by, realizes, create_edge, delete_edge, deploy_to, invalidates, pin_at_epoch). So the write family has ONE cost shape — ~120 ms of something every constructor does — and would be optimised as one class, not thirteen tools. Whether 120 ms is the search-index commit, the snapshot, the loop hint, or the schema guard is NOT measured here.

EVERYTHING ELSE IS ALREADY UNDER THE OBJECTIVE: get_skill 26 ms (18 KB), scan_nodes 44 ms (42 KB), create_edges 36 ms, describe_schema 2 ms (48 KB), what_next 77 ms, claim_report 44 ms warm. Reply SIZE is a second cost the timing does not see — detect_defects 58 KB, describe_schema 48 KB, scan_nodes 42 KB land in the agent's context on every call.

NOT MEASURED: graph_report (1.5-1.6 s, 41 calls), open_questions (1.27 s), what_next, and the 114 tools below the top 40 — 15% of calls. Absence in the transcript sample is weak evidence (the instrument's own caveat): a tool used before the retention window looks identical to one never used.
